name: Best Mistakes of Singletons
proof: For $n\geq2$, present any $n-1$ coordinates and predict $0$ at each. A positive label identifies its singleton target and causes one mistake; if all are negative, the unpresented coordinate is the target, with no mistake. Hence one mistake suffices. On the first presented coordinate, any learner prediction can be falsified: choose its singleton if it predicts $0$, and a different singleton if it predicts $1$. Thus one mistake is necessary. For $n=1$ the target is already known, so the value is zero.
